hypothesis: The parent's 0% joint accuracy comes from the model asking rows in order (A, then B, then C), using all 18 queries with about 6 rows never asked, and guessing those rows wrong (10/10 parent traces). If the parent's existing repeat-veto also blocks rows that the task rules (inventory, two AND/OR gates per circuit, NOTs anywhere, no constant circuit) plus the answers so far already decide, the model's own sequential queries land on informative rows and narrow every episode to a single joint table within 18 queries, so joint accuracy rises well above 0% on this batch.
behavior_changes: The harness enumerates the joint (A,B,C) tables allowed by the task rules and inventory, then keeps only those consistent with each answer.

A query on an unobserved row that every remaining table agrees on is vetoed and not counted (at most 3 times per turn). The re-ask names the forced value and lists the still-open rows. The repeat-veto list of 'inputs not asked yet' now shows only open rows.
Querying stops early once no row is open.
In the final 24-row table, forced rows show their value instead of '?'. The harness keeps observed and forced rows, and the model fills only truly open rows.
If the rules ever contradict an answer, or the inventory falls outside them (empty table set), the harness falls back to exactly the parent's behavior.
preserved_behaviors: Same single growing conversation with the benchmark system prompt, and the same per-turn wording ('<answer>\nPlease send your next query. N queries remaining.').
The model writes every query; repeat and missing-query re-asks work as before (MAX_RETRIES=6 per episode).
Final assembly as in the parent: observed rows always keep the environment's answer, '?' rows take the model's listed values or its <guess>, with one follow-up re-ask for missing rows.
verification: Replayed the parent's 10 recorded answer histories through the rule enumeration: all were consistent (nonempty set: 252 / 2886 / 3924 tables at the start, 1-5 at the end), which confirms the rules are read correctly. No truth tables were used.
Ran check_b0r1_cand_labeled6_b10g3r2_b0r1g0.py: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, joint truth table correct 10/10, circuit-wise 3/3 everywhere. Queries used: 7-17 (mean 11.9). No crashes.

Traces: 2-5 forced-row vetoes per episode, 0 repeat vetoes. Replaying the accepted queries showed 0 zero-information queries, and every episode ended with exactly 1 consistent table, so the final turn had 0 open rows.
risks: Correctness now depends on the harness reading the rules correctly. The replay supports it on this batch, and if an answer contradicts the rules the harness falls back to the parent.

In this batch the final bits all come from observed or rule-forced rows, so the model's fill step was never exercised. If an episode ended with several tables left, the model's '?' fill (weak in the parent traces) would decide the result.

The margin is thin on some instances (instance 250 used 17/18 queries). The model's sequential query order is not optimized, only steered away from rows that are already decided. If the per-turn veto cap of 3 runs out, a zero-information query is accepted, as in the parent.
Cost is close to the parent: 11-23 calls/episode; input tokens grow with the re-ask turns (up to 64k on instance 239).
